author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Uganda’s Tooro Kingdom prepared to bury King Oyo Nyimba on Saturday in Fort Portal after days of dispute over who should succeed him. Royal guards led a procession carrying his flag-draped casket from the palace to St. John’s Cathedral, where hundreds of mourners and senior government officials gathered before the burial at the royal tombs.

Oyo became internationally known in 1995 when he took the throne at age 3. He died in the United States in late August at 34 while receiving cancer treatment. During his reign he served as a United Nations goodwill ambassador and promoted efforts against HIV and AIDS, while the kingdom remained an important source of cultural identity in western Uganda.

A royal clan committee selected Oyo’s cousin Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma as king, but Oyo’s immediate family said a previously unknown son should inherit under the late monarch’s will. Supporters of Kijanangoma questioned whether enough information about the purported son had been produced. Ugandan authorities strengthened security as the kingdom moved ahead with the funeral and its traditional succession rites.
dek: The monarch who took the throne at age 3 is being laid to rest in Fort Portal after his death at 34 and a contested choice of successor.
headline: Uganda’s Tooro Kingdom buries King Oyo amid succession dispute
